title: Agent
description: What a kind of executor declares. `agent` spec §3.1. **Permissions are NOT here** — they live on the task, versioned with it (§3.2), because permission is a runtime fact about a particular piece of work rather than a property of a kind of executor.

description.description: What this kind of executor is for.

kind.description: Every task has exactly one agent, and what an agent IS is open (main spec §4.8). A `kind: program` agent is not a degenerate case: a large part of the reference workflow is running a command someone already wrote, and wrapping that in an AI would add cost and non-determinism for nothing.

backends.description:
For `kind: ai` — the implementations to try, **in order**, and the order is the preference (`agent` spec §3.3). A LIST, not a singleton: a backend either implements the interface or fails loudly, so the list is how a run survives one that cannot. A **mapping** whose keys are the `key`s is equally valid and is normalised to a list at load, preserving declaration order (design D2). No `uniqueItems`: an *identical* duplicate `key` is tolerated and a differing one is an error — matplotlib's entry-point rule, because duplicates arise from packaging outside the declarer's control — and that asymmetry is a model check, which `uniqueItems` would break by rejecting the identical case too.

`backends/claude_sdk.py` is never imported at module scope: the SDK is a 376 MB extra costing ~1.3 s to import, so a missing extra must be a `BackendUnsupported` naming it rather than an `ImportError` at start-up.

env.description: Environment requirements, resolved by `env_mgr`. **A package may name its own variables here, and this is the only route by which it can** — every other contributor to a task body's environment is derived by `env_mgr` itself (the policy-derived `PATH`, the staged-package variable, the grant-derived input and output variables, and the harness block). It is also the last merge and therefore wins over all of them: `env_mgr.prepare` applies `material.deploy` last, and `deploy` applies this block last within that, *"because an author saying so outranks a default"*. Not further constrained here: `env_mgr` owns the vocabulary and a schema in this repository would be a second declaration of it — that is about not writing a second schema, and says nothing about whose names may appear in the block.

knowledge.description: Knowledge arrives as knowledge HANDOFFS — versioned, digested, checkable — not as inline prose in a YAML file (`agent` spec §3.4). Missing knowledge is a warning by default and fatal under a run-config flag (§3.5): a hard requirement blocks bring-up, and a silent absence is how zero-shot agents happen.

kind.description: The knowledge handoff KIND's name — **not a handoff's name**. It must resolve in the handoff registry (§3.6 check 3).

knowledge_type.description: One of §3.4's six — `few_shot`, `runnable`, `official_reference`, `expert_experience`, `verifiable_resource`, `runtime_generated` — or a later one. Open on purpose rather than an enum: §3.4 says the list is extensible, and an enum would make the seventh type a code change in `agent`. The tokens are `agent/spec.py::KNOWLEDGE_TYPES`, which is what the coverage report enumerates.

required.description: **Load-bearing, and the only key that reconciles criteria 1 and 2.** A required ref whose kind does not resolve is fatal in *both* modes; a non-required one is fatal only under the run-config flag.

rules.description: Package-relative paths. Stored in canonical form (`agent` spec §4.5).

hooks.description: Package-relative paths. Stored in canonical form.

skills.description: Package-relative paths. Stored in canonical form.

assets.description:
This agent's own directory under `assets/`, package-relative. **Filled by convention, not written by hand** — `spec_loader/assets.py` matches the same three folder spellings the body lookup uses (`X`, `X.agent`, `agent.X`), and binding it explicitly is legal and warns. Two matching directories is `SpecInconsistent`.

It is where a package's **own** per-agent components live: `env_mgr` auto-detects `<assets>/.claude/` inside the STAGED copy of the package and installs what it finds — skills, hooks in `settings.json`, a local plugin marketplace, `.mcp.json`, and `tools/*.mcp.py` / `tools/*.tooldef.py`. Nothing declares them, because the declaration would be a second statement of what the directory already says. The staged directory also reaches the body as `AGENT_SYS_AGENT_ASSETS` and is copied into the attempt's workspace root as a subdirectory.

recipes.description:
**Components this repository does not ship**: `env_mgr` recipe YAMLs to run before the session starts, each installing things this repository does not ship (serena, marketplace plugins, apt/pip tools) — or, with an item carrying `tags: [internal]`, one that it does. A package-relative path, resolved against the STAGED package. Declared and absent is an error, for `material.py`'s measured reason: a skipped install surfaces hours later as `Unknown skill` from inside the agent's own session, with nothing naming the cause.

Run in declaration order, before `agent_plugins`, so a name a package ships wins a collision with one it merely asks for.

**This key is the AGENT layer of three.** Recipes come from three places and the layer is *where the file is*, never a field: `env_mgr/default.env_recipe.yaml` (the default — never declared, always applies), `<staged package>/assets/main.env_recipe.yaml` (the package's — never declared, auto-detected, and **that exact filename only**), and this key. They run most-general to most-specific and **concatenate**: a later layer ADDS items, it does not override an earlier one, which costs nothing because every installer gates on `check` before `install`. Nothing detects a version conflict *between* layers — see `agent_assets.py::_recipe_paths` for why, and what closing it would cost.

**May be filled by convention instead of written.** An agent that carries its own recipe names the file after itself under `assets/` — `env_recipe.<name>.yaml`, `<name>.env_recipe.yaml`, or any other `.`-joined permutation of the same tokens, including inside the agent's own `<name>.agent/` folder, where the name may be dropped. Scoped to `assets/`: a recipe at the package root is a load failure, because `_scan()` hands every `.yaml` outside `assets/` to the document discriminator. Two spellings for one agent is `SpecInconsistent`. Declaring this key by hand is legal, warns, and wins whole — the discovered path is not appended to a declared list.

agent_plugins.description: **The agent plugins this repository ships**: bare names under `agent_sys/agent_plugins/<name>/`, each holding a `.claude/` tree in the same on-disk shape as the one a package carries under `assets`, and optionally a `recipe.yaml` beside it for anything it must install first. One installer serves both precisely because the shape is the same; what differs is only who owns the directory. Declared and absent is an error.

key.description: The backend's name, resolved at run time. `claude_code_sdk`, `cursor_sdk`.

backend_entry.description: A dotted path `pkg.mod:Class` naming THIS exact one, or a bare entry-point name in group `agent_sys.backends`. Both forms are admitted; `agent` design §6.3 says why neither substitutes for the other. **Required**: it is what makes a declaration resolvable at all, and a spec carrying `key` alone would pass this gate and fail the model, putting the error one layer too late.

config.description: Backend-specific settings. Unconstrained: the vocabulary is the backend's.

err.description: The per-entry failure message. fsspec's `Install adlfs to access Azure Datalake Gen2` rather than a traceback about a missing submodule — the one thing a dotted string buys that an entry point cannot.
